name: Centaur Ear
summary: A centaur ear is taken as proof of a centaur slain in Desolace. Both the Horde and Alliance demand them as a sign of weakening the clans.

sections.title: A Grim Tally
sections.body: In Desolace, centaur ears are gathered for the Horde and Alliance alike. Felgur Twocuts asks Horde travelers for a great hoard, believing fewer centaur will weaken the clans' resolve. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins demands ears in service of the Alliance and its hope for peace. Both banners turn a grisly token into a measure of their struggle with the centaur.

faq.q: Why do they collect centaur ears?
faq.answer: Horde and Alliance officers use centaur ears as proof of slain centaur and as a tally meant to weaken the clans.

faq.q: Who wants centaur ears for the Horde?
faq.answer: Felgur Twocuts in Desolace asks Horde travelers to bring him a hoard of centaur ears.

faq.q: Who wants centaur ears for the Alliance?
faq.answer: Corporal Melkins at Nijel's Point asks Alliance travelers to bring him centaur ears.

faq.q: Do the clans matter which ears are taken from?
faq.answer: Felgur Twocuts says the Horde may hunt any centaur clan in Desolace.

angles.text: For the Horde, bringing ears to Felgur Twocuts is meant to weaken the centaur clans and mark the banner behind the bloodshed.
At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins calls the taking of centaur ears a service to the Alliance and a step toward peace.
